section: H "reference node" (the annex's only `shall`) / normative home 3.6.4, 1.3.1.1
title: 08 cannot fail: `gnd` sits at its default 0 bias, so a compiler that made ground an ordinary net prints the same 0.5 — and THE (singular) reference node is never pinned
detail: Annex H carries exactly one `shall` in the whole annex: "Nets declared as ground shall be bound to the reference node." 08 is the fixture for it and asserts nothing that can distinguish a conformant ground. VERIFIED BY RUNNING: contrary to the weak lens's stated mechanism ("gnd is not in D.U, lower.zig:565/codegen.zig:3029, so it cannot be biased"), `gnd` IS a solver unknown — the transcript prints `x[gnd]` — and `//! bias V(gnd) = 0.25` compiles and runs. lower.zig:565 maps every `is_ground` net to the sentinel index `ground`, which reads as a literal 0 (lower.zig:913), so the unknown exists but is never read. That makes the fix trivial and the fixture discriminating: bias the ground nets OFF zero and a compiler that treats `ground` as an ordinary net prints 0.25 where the LRM requires 0.5. Second half, also verified by running: two `ground` declarations in one module compile and both collapse to node 0, so the singular-article claim (THE reference node, not one per declaration) is writable here. Suite-wide it is untested — only ch01_intro/02_reference_ground.va, ch03_data_types/13_ground_declaration.va and this file declare a ground, all single-net. Also drop line 13's `CHECKR(V(p,gnd)/1000.0, 5e-4, 1e-15)`: it is line 12 divided by 1000 under a relative tolerance on a value that is exact, and it asserts nothing about the flow.

section: H (glossary-c, glossary-i, glossary-k, glossary-r, glossary-s, glossary-v)
title: The chapter's anti-conformant prose is all in COVERAGE.md: four rows write off normative terms as untestable by describing VerA's architecture, one of them falsified by a fixture that already exists
detail: Four separate false or implementation-shaped claims, one file, one edit. (a) glossary-k: "numerical KCL/KVL is outside syntax testing" is false — ch01_intro/08_series_potentials.va already asserts conservation of value around a loop with pure probe reads (`V(p,mid) + V(mid,n) == 1.5 == V(p,n)`), and ch01_intro/04_kirchhoff_flow_sum.va does the flow half. Do NOT write a new fixture; cite those. (b) glossary-c/glossary-i/glossary-s excuse child module / instance / instantiation / structural definitions with "hierarchy elaboration is non-codegen for a selected VerA device" and "VerA compiles the selected device definition, not a hierarchy" — that is a statement about the compiler, not about IEEE 1800-2023 §6.3, and the suite already asserts the opposite claim in annex_a_syntax/11_module_instantiation_rejected.va. State the gap as a gap (untested here, normative home §6.3/§6.4, owned by the ch06_hierarchy audit) instead of as a property of the standard. (c) glossary-r credits `04` with "reference direction", which 04 never asserts — do not touch this row until H-03 lands, then it becomes true. (d) "run time binding" (conditional introduction/removal of value and flow sources; a value source may replace a flow source) appears in no row at all; its normative home §5.6.5 is already covered by ch05_analog_behavior/switch_branch.va, so the fix is a row, not a fixture. Also worth one sentence at the top: the annex is informative and holds exactly one `shall`, so the chapter's conformance load is legitimately small — say that instead of inventing per-term excuses.
expected: glossary-k cites ch01_intro/08_series_potentials.va + 04_kirchhoff_flow_sum.va; glossary-c/i/s name §6.3/§6.4 and the owning chapter rather than VerA's codegen; a `run time binding` entry citing §5.6.5 and ch05_analog_behavior/switch_branch.va; the word VerA appears nowhere as a justification for a term being untestable.

section: H "branch" / "reference direction" (PDF p.433 l.29-31, p.435 l.170-172)
title: 04 is the chapter's reference-direction fixture and never reverses anything — a compiler that ignores branch orientation passes it
detail: The glossary defines a branch as carrying "a value and a flow, WITH A REFERENCE DIRECTION FOR EACH", and COVERAGE.md glossary-r credits 04 with exactly that. 04 asserts only `V(b) == 0.5`. The one line that would make it a direction test — the negation under reversal — is carried by three other chapters (ch05_analog_behavior/potential_probe.va:13 has `V(n,p) == -0.5`) and is missing here; without it 04 is a strictly weaker copy of that ch05 fixture. Line 13's `CHECKR("branch flow from the constitutive relation", V(b)/1000.0, 5e-4, 1e-15)` is not a flow assertion at all: it is line 12 divided by 1000, evaluated in the check itself, never read back from the solver, and its value is exact so the relative tolerance is decoration. Replace it with the named/unnamed identity, which is the claim the named-branch declaration actually adds.

title: 07 has one assertion, it is the same claim 04 and ch05_analog_behavior/potential_probe.va already make, and it tests neither the flow half nor the does-not-alter half of the definition
detail: Annex H: "a branch in a circuit which DOES NOT ALTER ITS BEHAVIOR, but lets the simulator read out the potential OR FLOW at that point." 07 reads a potential and contributes it back as a flow, which is the opposite of not altering. Its single `CHECKX(..., 0.5)` restates 04:12 and ch05_analog_behavior/potential_probe.va:12 (not verbatim — the labels differ — but the same value from the same bias). The flow half is writable and I ran it: hold the branch flow with the same `//! sweep` spelling ch01_intro/10_flow_probe.va already uses and `I(probe_branch)` reads it back. The does-not-alter half is visible in the transcript rather than in a macro: with the contribution moved off the probed branch the runner prints `res[flowZ28pZ2cnZ29] = 0`. Cheaper alternative if the author does not want a third probe fixture in the suite: delete 07 and give glossary-p a row citing ch01_intro/09_potential_probe.va and 10_flow_probe.va — that is the honest zero-diff option and it loses nothing.

title: 09 pins limexp() to exp() on a single un-iterated residual evaluation; 4.5.13 guarantees that identity at convergence and leaves the limiting algorithm open
detail: Verified against the LRM text: 4.5.13 says limexp "has internal state containing information about the argument on previous iterations", "internally limits the change of its output from iteration to iteration", and "the simulator can only converge when the output of limexp() EQUALS the exponential of the input" — the identity is a property of the converged point, and "there are different ways of implementing limiting algorithms". (The same clause also says the apparent behavior "is not distinguishable from exp()", which is why this is medium and not high.) The runner evaluates the residual once, cold, at V(p,n)=0.1; a conforming implementation with SPICE-style pnjlim seeding returns a limited value on that first evaluation and fails a numeric want it is entitled to miss. The values themselves are right — I recomputed 4.6855e-13 against all five Annex D constant sets and it is the midpoint of 4.685467e-13..4.686029e-13 — so this is a claim problem, not a digit problem.
expected: Assert the value through `exp(V(p,n)/$vt)` (which the LRM does pin) and keep `limexp` only in the contribution: `CHECKR("diode law at 100 mV", saturation*(exp(V(p,n)/$vt) - 1.0), 4.6855e-13, 1e-3); I(p,n) <+ saturation*(limexp(V(p,n)/$vt) - 1.0);`. The zero-bias line may keep limexp: exp(0)-1 == 0 holds under any limiter.

title: 06 asserts V(internal_node,terminal_n) == 0.125 while the same module contributes V(internal_node,terminal_n) <+ 0.375
detail: Both numbers are arithmetically correct for the pinned bias — the runner does one residual evaluation and never solves, so the assertion holds — but the fixture asserts a point its own constitutive relation forbids. Confirmed by running it: the transcript prints `res[flowZ28internal_nodeZ2cterminal_nZ29] = -2.5e-1`, i.e. exactly the 0.125-0.375 inconsistency, printed right underneath an ok=1. The claim being made ("an internal node is an unknown of its own") is worth keeping and is true; it just needs a bias that is a solution of the module rather than one contradicted by it, and it needs the internal node's value to differ from both terminals so the claim still discriminates.
expected: Weaken the contribution to a fraction and pin the consistent bias, e.g. `V(internal_node,terminal_n) <+ 0.5*V(terminal_p,terminal_n);` with `//! bias V(terminal_p)=0.5, V(terminal_n)=0.125, V(internal_node)=0.3125`, then `CHECKX("the port pair's potential", V(terminal_p,terminal_n), 0.375)` and `CHECKX("an internal node is an unknown of its own", V(internal_node,terminal_n), 0.1875)` — distinct from both terminals AND a zero-residual point. All values exact in binary64.

section: 3.4 (parameter constancy), via glossary "parameter" — normative home ch03_data_types
title: The glossary defines a parameter as "A constant" and nothing in 857 fixtures pins constancy: E0312 is cited by zero fixtures
detail: Verified twice: `grep -rn 'E0312' tests/fixtures` is empty, and the diagnostic really does fire — `parameter real gain = 2.0; analog begin gain = 3.0; ... end` gives `error[E0312]: cannot assign to a parameter: gain` with `note: LRM 3.4`. So the rule is implemented and unpinned; a refactor that dropped the check would break no fixture. Filed against ch03_data_types, not annex_h: Annex H is informative and the enforceable rule lives in 3.4 (E0312's own catalogue entry cites 3.4). Next free number in that directory is 43 and its reject fixtures pair a `//! reject` line with an `.expected-error.txt`.

section: 9.15 / Annex D constants (09's wants and its cite)
title: 09's header comment overstates the diode agreement, does not record either tolerance floor, and cites $vt to the wrong clause
detail: Both wants are numerically right — I recomputed them independently across all five Annex D constant sets at T=300: $vt spans 0.025851241..0.025852027 (want 0.025852 is the midpoint, worst relative error 2.94e-5 against an rtol of 1e-4, 3.4x margin) and the diode current spans 4.685467e-13..4.686029e-13 (want 4.6855e-13, worst relative error 1.13e-4 against an rtol of 1e-3, 8.8x margin). Three cosmetic defects around them: the comment says the current "holds to four digits" when 4.6855 vs 4.6860 already differ in the fourth digit; neither want records that it is a midpoint of a constant-set spread nor the rtol floor it needs (3.0e-5 and 1.2e-4), so a later tightening of the tolerance would look safe and would not be; and "$vt is kT/q (§4.5.14)" cites "Constant versus dynamic arguments" — $vt is 9.15 Analog Kernel Parameter System Functions, Syntax 9-10. Verified all three against docs/VAMS-LRM/ch4-expressions.html and ch9-system.html.
expected: Comment reads: want = midpoint of the Annex D spread; rtol must stay above 3.0e-5 ($vt) and 1.2e-4 (diode); cite §9.15 for $vt. No CHECK line changes value.

title: 01 cites a clause that does not exist (§4.4.1) and attributes procedural assignment to §5.2
detail: Verified against docs/VAMS-LRM/ch4-expressions.html and ch5-analog.html: 4.4 is "Signal access functions" and has no subsections at all, so §4.4.1 is unresolvable — the node-pair-difference claim belongs to 4.4 itself (Table 4-16). §5.2 is "Analog procedural block"; analog procedural assignment is §5.7. Both wants in the file are correct (V(p,n)=0.5, intermediate=1.0, exact in binary64); this is a two-token comment fix.
expected: Header cites §4.4 (Table 4-16) for the potential probe and §5.7 for procedural assignment.

section: 5.3.2 / 6.8 (block scope), via glossary "scope", "block", "nesting level" — normative home ch05_analog_behavior
title: Nothing in the suite checks that a block-item declaration is INVISIBLE outside its begin-end; only the two permissive directions are tested
detail: ch05_analog_behavior/named_block_locals.va tests that a block-local is usable inside its block and ch06_hierarchy/local_scope_shadow.va tests that the enclosing scope stays visible inside — neither tests the restrictive direction the glossary's "scope" and "nesting level" entries describe. CORRECTION to the uncovered lens: it asks for E0313, and E0313 is indeed the code whose explain text advertises this exact case ("a name declared inside a named block (LRM 5.3.2) is not visible outside it"), but the compiler actually emits E0314 ("unknown identifier") — I ran it. Write the fixture against E0314, and note that E0313 is still cited by zero fixtures suite-wide, which is a separate question for whoever owns that diagnostic. E0314 today is pinned by exactly one fixture, ch04_expressions/103_function_nonlocal_variable.va, which is analog-function scope, not begin-end scope.
expected:
//! reject E0314
`analog begin begin : inner real hidden; hidden = V(p); end out = hidden; ... end` plus a matching .expected-error.txt containing `E0314`. Verified: current engine reports `error[E0314]: unknown identifier: hidden`.

title: 03's header restates two glossary definitions with the halves it does not test silently removed
detail: The annex says control flow is "the CONDITIONAL AND ITERATIVE statements controlling the behavior of a module"; 03 says "the conditional statements selecting a section of the description" and drops the iterative half without saying so. Same shape for "block": the annex's "level"/"nesting level" entries say a level is delimited by "a pair of matching keywords SUCH AS begin-end OR discipline-enddiscipline"; 03 says "a level delimited by begin-end". A comment that quotes a narrowed definition reads as if the fixture covered it. No assertion changes: 03's `CHECKI(V(p,n) > 0.0, 0)` and `CHECKX(result, 0.4)` are both correct at bias -0.4.
expected: Header states the full definitions and names what this fixture covers (the conditional half, begin-end delimitation) and what it does not (the iterative half — covered by the ch05 loop fixtures; discipline-enddiscipline as a level).

title: No fixture carries a `//! lrm` cite, although every header names its clause in prose and the directive exists
detail: The directive is real and validated — src/backend/tb.zig parses `//! lrm <section>` through validSection() and documents it as "what lets a FAIL name the RULE that broke rather than only the file, and what a coverage report counts". Zero fixtures use it. IMPORTANT CAVEAT the weak lens missed: this is true of all 857 fixtures in the suite, not of this chapter — `grep -rl '//! lrm' tests/fixtures` is empty. So this is a suite-wide convention decision (adopt it everywhere or delete the directive), not an Annex H defect, and it should not be done here alone unless the chapter is being used as the pilot. Ranked last for that reason.
expected: If adopted: `//! lrm 4.4` on 01, `3.4` on 02 and 05, `5.3` on 03, `5.6.1` on 04, `3.6.3` on 06, `5.4.2` on 07, `3.6.4` on 08, `4.5.13` on 09 — matching the clause each header already names in prose.
